entries.core_move: Recognize time invariance by interpreting whether delaying or advancing any continuous-time input causes the system output to undergo the identical delay or advance without changing shape or rule.
Compute the output produced by first shifting a continuous-time input signal and then applying the system rule, so it can be compared against the system-then-shift path in a time-invariance test.
Compute the system-then-shift path by applying the continuous-time system rule to $x(t)$ to get $y(t)$, then replacing t with t - T to form $y(t - T)$ for comparison in a time-invariance test.
Compare the shift-then-system and system-then-shift expressions for an arbitrary input shift to classify a continuous-time input-output system as time invariant or time varying.

Apply the time-invariance shift test to memoryless continuous-time system rules by verifying that the fixed pointwise mapping from $x(t)$ to $y(t)$ commutes with input shifts and contains no explicit dependence on t.
Compare the shift-then-system and system-then-shift outputs for system rules containing explicit $t$ to recognize when absolute-time dependence makes a continuous-time system time varying.

Distinguish time invariance from signal shifting by tracing the shift-then-system and system-then-shift paths to decide whether a continuous-time system preserves input delays as identical output delays.
